generator.why: Rows of 8 to 48 features with x within ±100 and a spread of at least 0.5, and gamma and dy within ±3. The numpy generator lets a row's spread fall to 0.01 (or, with 2 features, two nearby values: 39.48 and 39.54), with gamma and dy up to 10, so dx reaches 1e4 and float32's cancellation error swamps its small entries. Stored cases keep the full range, down to 1 feature.

skip.large-mean-tiny-spread: A mean of 1000 with a spread of 0.05: float32 rounds the mean itself by more than the answer can absorb, so even the two-pass formula is off by ~1e-3. torch-large-mean-small-spread keeps the trap at float32 scale (mean 100, spread ~3), where two-pass passes and one-pass E[x²] − E[x]² still fails.
